memory_verse: "He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit." —Romans 8:11, NASB
sermon_title: A Freedom Only Christ Can Give

days.focus: External vs. Internal: What Does God Really See?
days.reflection_question: If God were to issue a 'certificate' for your inner life this past week — your thoughts, motives, and attitudes — what would it say?
days.application: At the end of the day, take five minutes in a quiet place and honestly list two or three things from your inner life this week that only God has seen. Acknowledge them before Him in prayer.
days.memory_verse_practice: Read Romans 8:11 aloud slowly three times from your Bible, paying attention to each phrase. Write the verse out once in your journal or on a notecard.

days.focus: Captives Who Look Free: The Bondage Beneath the Surface
days.reflection_question: In what area of your inner life — anger, lust, bitterness, anxiety, pride — do you feel most like a captive, even while appearing fine on the outside?
days.application: Write a one-sentence honest prayer to God about one specific internal bondage you have been covering up. Keep it somewhere private as a reminder that you have brought it before Him.
days.memory_verse_practice: Read Romans 8:11 aloud three times, then try to write it out from memory without looking. Check your version against the text and correct any mistakes. Focus on the phrase 'will give life to your mortal bodies.'

days.focus: Freedom Christ Gives That the Law Cannot: Acts 13 and the Gospel
days.reflection_question: In what ways have you been relying on external rules, routines, or willpower to manage your inner life rather than turning to Christ for genuine freedom?
days.application: The next time you feel an internal struggle today — an angry thought, an envious feeling, a fearful anxiety — stop and say aloud: 'Christ, I cannot free myself from this. I am asking You to set me free, as Acts 13:39 promises.'
days.memory_verse_practice: Without looking, try to recite Romans 8:11 aloud twice. Then read it once from the text to confirm accuracy. Write it out again, this time breaking it into three natural phrases and memorizing the structure: (1) 'He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead' / (2) 'will give life to your mortal bodies' / (3) 'through His Spirit.'

days.focus: Do You Wish to Be Well? Honesty Before the Physician
days.reflection_question: Like the man at Bethesda, have you quietly settled for your condition — stopped truly expecting or asking God to change your inner life? What would it look like to say 'yes' to Jesus's question today?
days.application: Spend ten minutes in prayer specifically telling God that you want to be made well on the inside — not just appear well to others. Name the specific struggle you identified on Tuesday and ask Him directly for the life and freedom that His Spirit can bring.
days.memory_verse_practice: Recite Romans 8:11 from memory three times without looking — once quietly, once at a normal speaking pace, once as if explaining it to someone else. Write it out one more time, this time from complete memory, and keep the card or paper visible today.

days.focus: His Spirit Gives Life: The Power Behind the Freedom
days.reflection_question: Romans 8:11 says the same Spirit who raised Jesus from the dead lives in you. Does your daily inner life reflect someone who believes that kind of resurrection power is available to them right now?
days.application: Choose one practical moment today — a conversation, a decision, a temptation — and consciously pause before it, reminding yourself: 'The Spirit that raised Christ lives in me.' Act from that reality rather than from habit or fear.
days.memory_verse_practice: Recite Romans 8:11 completely from memory without any aids, three times at different points in the day — morning, afternoon, and evening. Notice which words still feel uncertain and review only those words once from the text.

days.focus: From the Inside Out: Living for God's Opinion, Not Man's
days.reflection_question: As you look back across the week, have you made any shift — even a small one — from caring most about what others see externally to caring about what God sees internally? What is one concrete thing you want to carry into Sunday and the week ahead?
days.application: Do one act of genuine inner obedience today that no one else will see or know about — forgive someone privately in your heart, resist an internal sin without telling anyone, or serve quietly without recognition — and offer it to God as worship from the inside of the cup.
days.memory_verse_practice: Recite Romans 8:11 from complete memory — no notes, no Bible — and then write it out one final time in full. Read it aloud one last time slowly, meditating on every word, so that you carry it into Sunday's service fully memorized and personally owned.
